symbols.label: Acceptance: the decision owner's disposition over an unchanged subject, exhausting only the instance and interval it names

Activated frame: one frame declaration bound to an exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary; a reusable declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct

Activation packet: the minimum an actor receives on activation: one activated frame or one declared active frame configuration with its identity, evaluation, subject, relations, authorities, evidence, envelope, exclusions, dependencies and stop conditions
Active frame configuration: the set of frame activations and declared result relations used for one evaluation or decision; one frame or several disjoint, overlapping or composed frames
Actor: whoever performs a step within a declared capability envelope (context, attention, time, capability)
Actor identity: the human, agent, tool or process performing the work; an identity, not an authority
Admission: the relation that validates a drafted step contract against its cited basis and admits it for execution; distinct from drafting even inside one invocation
Allowance: declared resource bound and spend measurement where capability fit or cost is the governed question
Applicability: the determination, from the owning evaluation and scope declarations and sufficient basis-bound facts, of which frame obligations apply to the exact subject
Applicability check: the check an unchanged consumer performs before reusing a closed result
Independent assessment protocol: freeze, expectations, named identity, no repair, no own authorship
Assessor: the relation that evaluates a frozen candidate independently

Assurance independence (claim-relative): the non-authorship, evidence-acquisition, reference-exposure, actor and configuration separation the governing assurance law requires for a verdict to count as independent assurance

Authority: an identity-bearing permission to operate or to dispose acceptance within a scope; never minted from capability, label or reachability; its kinds are frame-set, semantic, evaluation, operation and decision authority

Basis: the exact state a step, claim, result or evaluation binds: every version, identity, time, topology, authority, configuration or evidence coordinate whose change can alter it; immutable, or moving with a declared way of detecting advancement and a declared reevaluation condition; mixed bases need an explicit composite relation
Candidate: a step's output before evaluation
Carrier of a work item: durable ticket, sprint-local entry, or run or return record
Change class: goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice, design_reframe or realization_refactor, each with its re-entry point
Checker: a mechanical decider of the structural subset
Checkpoint: the exact state acceptance binds
Churn: rejected or superseded construction
Claim: an assertion with subject, property, basis, witness relation and falsifier

Disposition of a predecessor claim in this corpus (UP-015 applied to the corpus itself): conserved, superseded, intentionally removed, not applicable with a bounded reason, or unresolved; a reframing note is commentary on the carrying, never a disposition

Closed result: identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual uncertainty and the invalidation conditions; minimal shape REFERENCE_FRAME section 13; available for reuse under an applicability check
Closure condition: the condition a work item stated for its own closure
Independently activated co-evaluation: several frames evaluate the same subject through separate activations and return closed results
Standing of a commitment relative to the others: recovered, derived, independent or hypothesis

Completeness boundary: without an independently established closed-domain completeness predicate, a finite frame set cannot establish the absence of undiscovered material evaluations from its own inventory
Composition of steps s2 after s1
Admitted condition class with a declared disposition, including an explicit unknown class
Conformance: a realisation's interpreted behaviour satisfies a specification under a declared interpretation contract and an independent judgment
Conformance case: subject, mechanism under test, independently specified expected distinction, status
Transformation record: preserved, introduced, removed, external resolution witnesses, residuals
The chain Goals, Intent, Product Definition, Requirements, Design and realisation, Code or documents, Events, Projection, Delta, Scenarios, Gap analysis, Repricing
Constructor: the relation that produces the candidate and self-review
Context: the declared scope under which an interpretation holds (subject, definitions, basis, admissible observations)
Contract state: drafted, admitted, rejected or superseded

Coordinate: the complete local position from which a value, event, decision, observation or action is interpreted (basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence, authority); equal names, values, shapes or apparent positions do not establish coordinate equality, which follows a declared relation
Evidence or coordinate translation: one frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another through a declared mapping
The ten core claims of REFERENCE_FRAME section 2, made precise by the laws of section 3

The method's core statement: interpret a scoped subject; select a purpose and governing contract; transform within admitted authority while conserving its material relations; evaluate the resulting claims; continue, recover or conclude from current state under explicit uncertainty
Cost categories kept separate: startup, framework, external computation, transport, assurance
Counterexample case from the builder's own history, naming the mechanism that must catch it
Required obligation set R, admitted coverage C and uncovered coverage R minus C

Coverage dimension: a cross-cutting lens applied to the inventory (outcome and capability; identity and authority; lifecycle and temporal behaviour; topology and seams; transport and representation; evidence and proof; change, failure, recovery and rollback; historical regression; actor capability and context fit)

Coverage ledger: one row per evaluation with evaluation, provenance, subject and basis, selected frames, actor envelope, semantic authority, operation authority, decision authority, evidence, dependencies, status and residual
Coverage status: covered, separately_covered, conditionally_covered, conflicted, uncovered, unknown or excluded_by_authority
Coverage tuple Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T): workspace, governed outcome, exact basis, known evaluation inventory, declared frame set, and the time or immutable checkpoint of the claim
Decision authority: the role permitted to accept, reject or otherwise dispose a result
Decision owner: the relation that disposes

Decision rule: states which results are mandatory, how conflict and indeterminacy are handled, which basis relations must agree, which decision authority owns the conjunction, and whether any result may veto or defer
Diagnostic order: the eight questions asked in order before another frame is created
Named dispositions after a non-satisfied result: continue within the contract, refine, recover, yield, re-enter the owning relation, terminate
Document map: the seven law documents (FOUNDATIONS, REFERENCE_FRAME, ACTIVATION, EVALUATION, SPEC_METHOD, CONFORMANCE, PROFILES), their tiers and what each owns
Engagement atom: a frame is atomic at engagement altitude (activated and evaluated as one bounded attention unit); semantic irreducibility is a separate question

Capability envelope K (envelope B of ACTIVATION section 2): the competence, context capacity, tools, access, applicable independence conditions and configuration required to activate a frame; usable by one actor and not another; it can neither waive an invariant nor widen authority

Evaluation: a declared question whose admissible result family, evidence basis, decision authority and, where it performs a material action, operation authority are known; may ask for a judgment, prediction, construction, comparison, proof, refusal, classification or action recommendation
Evaluation authority: the role permitted to perform an evaluation
Evaluation family: evaluations that need the same material-relation manifold, authority basis and result algebra; similar wording proves no shared family

Evaluation independence (procedural): separately activated evaluations neither consume nor influence one another's unclosed working results, though they may inspect the same subject, overlap and later supply closed results to one conjunction
Evaluation inventory: the known material evaluations of a workspace and outcome, derived from every material available source, with provenance and materiality recorded
Evaluator: the relation that applies the declared relation between law and evidence

Evidence: the exact observations or artifacts admitted to evaluate a claim on a basis, each with provenance, subject identity, basis and scope; availability inside a frame makes it neither semantic truth nor decision authority
Executive relation: the declared consumer of returns in a coordinated configuration; selects the next already-authorised action
External test subject: a worked application, hello world or data mapper whose particulars cannot become generic method functionality
Falsifier: the observation that would defeat a claim, named before a witness is selected
Finding: an evidence-bearing item of a review with its smallest bounded correction
Fit test of the selected context against the envelope
The established categorical fragment: free category A on typed primitives, carrier sets I, cost pairs C_H, functors S and R_H
Closure under REFERENCE_FRAME: the eight conditions under which a project operates under the member
Frame disjointness (structural): two frames share no material variable, coordinate, evidence or result dependency for the declared evaluations
Frame qualification: the nine-test minimum evaluation of a candidate frame, in proportion to its claims
Frame relation: disjoint, overlapping, complementary, alternative, refinement, restriction, translated, temporally successive, composed, or governing and subordinate

Frame set: the human-declared family of frames available for a governed outcome or workspace; may hold overlaps, alternatives, specialist, exploratory and separately activated assurance frames; not required to be a partition, tree, stack or exhaustive ontology
Frame-set authority: the human authority that declares or accepts a project frame set

Frame-set declaration: the human-declared record of workspace and outcome, evaluation inventory, selected frames and envelopes, overlaps, dependencies and translations, authorities, exclusions and residual uncertainty, and revision conditions
Frame-set selection: a constrained coverage problem over the known material evaluations E(W, G) of workspace W and governed outcome G

The frame tuple F = (Q evaluation family, B workspace and topology basis, M manifold, C coordinate and equality law, I invariants, A authority relation, E evidence and provenance law, X exclusions and prohibited assumptions, R closed result algebra, J invalidation and rechart condition, K actor capability envelope, D declared dependencies, overlaps, inputs and outputs with other frames)
Frame violation: one of the fourteen patterns that violate REFERENCE_FRAME where it supports a frame or coverage claim
Method function activate(frame, evaluation, subject, basis, actor) -> activated_frame | activation_refusal; ACTIVATION sections 1 to 3
Method function audit_coverage(workspace, outcome, evaluation_inventory, frame_set) -> coverage_ledger; section 8
Method function conjoin(decision_rule, frame_results) -> decision | conflict | indeterminate; section 6
Method function declare(human_authority, workspace, outcome, practices, capabilities) -> frame_set; section 4
Method function evaluate(activated_frame, admissible_evidence) -> result + evidence + residuals; ACTIVATION sections 3 and 7
Method function revise(frame_set, new_evidence, failures, capability_change, topology_change) -> proposed_frame_set_delta; section 10
Method function translate(source_frame, target_frame, value_or_evidence, mapping) -> translated_value | declared_loss | refusal; section 6
Grant: operations permitted, territory that may change, decisions reserved to others
Graph execution profile: binds the step to one vector or edge traversal and the roles to F_P, F_D and F_H
Hypothesis: categorical equivalence of A and I under some reformulation
Hypothesis: traversal composition laws of any runtime
Hypothesis: the statistical boundary construct at candidate status
Hypothesis: universal algorithmic capture of meaning
Hard stop: a condition that stops regardless of risk appetite
Declared policy on whether two activations of one actor family are independent for a semantic judgment

Intake: the activation record from which a step's governing relations are reconstructed without history; names the governed outcome, exact subject and basis with inputs by identity, the evaluation and its algebra, the affected relation set, the applicable authorities and the grant, the actor envelopes, staleness and re-entry conditions, and where governed the allowance
Interpretation: a declared contract from representation to meaning within a context
Invalidator: a changed material input, basis or declared revising observation that invalidates a result before reliance
Judgment: a recorded evaluation over an unchanged subject, with evaluator, decision, evidence, scope and revising observation
A declared latitude or transformation relation under which two values may differ lawfully
Compression that preserves the material distinctions and failure detections the evaluation needs
A layer of the chain; sufficient when a competent actor can derive a conformant next layer

Lens: a reusable family of questions applied across a frame configuration (authority, capability, temporal behaviour, transport, proof when named abstractly); becomes a frame only when instantiated with a bounded evaluation, basis, manifold, evidence, authorities, result algebra and capability envelope
Major ambiguity: ambiguity that changes architecture, boundary, admissibility or public contract

Material: of a relation, that its lawful change can change an evaluation's result, invalidate its basis, change the admissible evidence, or change who may perform a material operation or decide; evaluation-relative, so a relation material in one frame may be irrelevant in another
Material closure of Z under R on the exact basis
Material composition: several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning relation, declared by the owning application

Material-relation manifold M: the finite, jointly interpretable set of variables, entities, identities, states, relations, invariants, authorities, observations and exclusions an evaluation family needs; charts may overlap; no geometry or runtime abstraction is implied
The comparative baseline's criteria F27 to F30: native representation, onboarding, effectiveness evidence, work and resource measurement
Qualification of the method itself: a fresh constructor inside a declared envelope, then an independent evaluator against the mandatory relation population
Migration: the change path for a load-bearing shared contract

Minimal activation binding: the carrier-neutral content sufficient to bind one declared frame for one evaluation, under the headings Frame; Subject And Basis; Attention Surface; Actor And Authority; Evidence And Relations; Stop And Change
Minimal evaluation result: the twelve fields that close one frame evaluation
Minimal frame declaration: the least content that declares a frame, twelve sections from Evaluation Family to Qualification
Minimal frame-set declaration: nine sections from Governed Workspace And Outcome to Revision Triggers
Missing-frame signal: an observation that triggers frame diagnosis
Object O: a subject with scoped identity (authority, kind, value), boundary, current state and declared material relations
Operation authority: the owner-issued grant to construct, transform, admit, publish or mutate a material subject where an evaluation performs such an operation; a read-only evaluation declares none
Operational full coverage: the eight conditions under which a frame set fully covers its declared tuple; relative to the tuple, never a claim that no undiscovered evaluation exists
Outcome U: a selected, owner-defined, directly verifiable state with an acceptance interval
Outer contract: a transformation T: A -> X with success predicates P0 ... Pn that steps refine
P0 Bounded construction
P1 Interpretation
P2 Purpose
P3 Identity
P4a Typed composition
P4b Conservation of step-produced facts
P5 Totality
P6 Justification and authority
Disposition of a predecessor claim: conserved, superseded, intentionally removed, or not applicable with a bounded reason
Preservation checkpoint: retention of unfinished work under an existing grant
Product roles: source project, release cut, product, install, artifact, development product
Profile: a domain extension that adds obligations, bindings and vocabulary and imports the core by reference
Profile binding: a declared binding of a core mechanism to a profile term, with direction, preserved meaning, narrowed scope and invalidation
Progress: accepted material movement toward the selected outcome
Proportionality: the relation between semantic ambiguity removed and effective reasoning complexity introduced
Proxy: an explicitly admitted bounded relation through which a human decision is exercised
Qualification population: every method function and failure relation the method claims, each with its required representative observations
falsified: a declared counterexample defeats it
indeterminate: admissible evidence cannot decide it
invalid_basis: the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation
out_of_frame: the evaluation needs an undeclared material relation or capability
satisfied: the declared predicate holds on the exact basis
The rc.2 builder corpus whose clauses this corpus conserves, reframes or supersedes
Reading route: for a stated purpose, the documents and sections to read in order
Reconfiguration: the disposition that follows an out_of_frame, invalid_basis, repeated indeterminate or incompatible result

Recoverability benchmark: whether a fresh actor given only the published documents recovers the governing relations, with fidelity judged independently and reconstruction cost measured against the rc.2 baseline
Recoverability case: a fresh actor given only this corpus, with private knowledge withheld
A reference standing for a relation in place of its body

Reference frame: a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations required to perform one declared evaluation family over a stated basis; its components are the frame tuple
Faithful refinement of an outer transformation into steps T_i
Refinement: ambiguity outcome (resolved, carried, escalated, blocked)
Refinement: construction availability (candidate_ready, refused, incomplete, re_entry_requested)
Refinement: disposition (accept, local_repair, re_enter, reject)
Refinement: profile-defined closure decisions
Relation family R: dependency relations whose change can alter the result, basis validity, evidence sufficiency or authority
Representation: bytes, text, a model or a program standing for a subject
Residual: a material uncertainty, omission, loss or unproven relation that remains until an authorised disposition
Restart: a proposed reconstruction from less than the retained work
The one core result algebra for every evaluation and stop state
Result conjunction: a declared decision rule consumes closed frame results
Resumption: re-entry of the same method over current work state by a possibly different actor
Review result: one core result per declared predicate with subject, basis, evidence, ranked findings, residual uncertainty, invalidation conditions and a recommended disposition
Revision action: a lawful change to a frame set in response to evidence, failure, capability change or topology change
RF-001 Evaluation relativity: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-002 Finite attention: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-003 Material sufficiency: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-004 Irrelevance exclusion: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-005 Exact basis and coordinates: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-006 Authority conservation: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-007 Semantic, evidence and verdict separation: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-008 Overlap without identity collapse: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-009 No assumed hierarchy: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-010 Composition on demand: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-011 Topology mutation and recharting: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-012 Closed results: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-013 Reconstructable activation: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-014 Capability fit: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-015 Residual uncertainty: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-016 Implementation neutrality: a law every declared or activated frame obeys
RF-017 Proportional compression: a law every declared or activated frame obeys

Role, persona, abstraction, component: a role allocates responsibility or authority, a persona alters salience, an abstraction contracts detail, a component is a structural part; each may help construct or activate a frame and none is a reference frame by identity alone
Seam: a relation crossing the boundary of the affected set
Seed set Z: subject, outcome and affected relations named in the intake
Selected context: the projection of the closure with its recorded boundary seams
Self-review: a constructor's own review of its candidate
Semantic authority: the owner of meaning for a material relation
Semantic fidelity: meaning and materiality
Semantic law: what an evaluation means
One implementation serving many instances
The shared constitutional WHAT located by a product definition's what bindings
Software design profile: binds the ontology-first derivation chain and the design laws
Specification Σ: the contract a realisation is judged to conform to
Steel thread: the smallest real path from a supported entry to a material outcome, widened by increments
Step: one bounded unit of work (intake, selected context, grant, execution, output); the activation of one reference frame, or one declared active frame configuration, on an exact subject
Step-produced fact: a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision produced by a step that cannot be re-acquired from declared sources; a reproducible observation is not one
Stop state: the one core result a step returns
Structural conformance: closed syntax, types, identities, references, bases and mechanically decidable predicates
Subject: the thing a claim, representation or transformation is about; exact, with inventory and bytes or semantic addresses
Successor: a cut that names the exact predecessor immutable cut whose claims it evolves
An independent realisation (HOW) located by a product definition's how.build_tenants bindings; derivative until its governing truth is ratified

Topology: the relation structure among material entities, capabilities, authorities, lifecycle state spaces, adjacencies and seams visible to a frame at one basis; a transition that changes any of them is a topology mutation that may invalidate the frame's coordinates
Intake triage: change intent, class, re-entry point and when triage occurred
Trial case from the comparative baseline with a shared task and expected distinction
UX profile: binds reader and task obligations, operational projection and screen-level acceptance
Witness: the evidence selected to support a claim under a declared relation
Work state: current persistent workspace, governing basis, applicable closed results and judgments with their invalidators, residuals, and known uncertainty over external effects
Work wave: the current bounded selection of outcome-bearing work

Workspace: the bounded body of material reasoned over or acted upon (sources, assets, designs, implementations, tools, runtime state, evidence, history, dependencies, human decisions); broader than a repository, which is one carrier
World model profile: binds entity recovery, the entity cut, the attribute ledger, composition and the Markov-object construct at candidate status

arguments.literal: A frame name, an available tool or a listed family triggers no activation by itself. Where applicability needs residual semantic judgment, that judgment and its evidence are retained as a judgment, never represented as a computed fact.
P6, P1

clauses.statement: A frame name, tool or listed family triggers no activation; residual semantic judgment in applicability stays a recorded judgment, never a computed fact.

arguments.literal: A required result that is absent, stale, bound to another subject or basis, or incapable of establishing its claim cannot satisfy a dependent conjunction; unresolved applicability withholds the dependent claim until sufficient evidence or the owning decision resolves it; other applicable constraints stay in force even if only one evaluation detects them.
P4b, P5

clauses.statement: An absent, stale, wrong-subject or incapable required result cannot satisfy a dependent conjunction; unresolved applicability withholds the dependent claim; other constraints stay in force.

arguments.literal: Acceptance binds one exact checkpoint and does not widen the outcome; the next already-authorised step may begin without renewed human approval when basis, affected set, decision envelope and re-entry conditions are already accepted; direct human acceptance is not weakened where Product or release law requires it.

clauses.statement: Acceptance binds one checkpoint and does not widen the outcome; an already-authorised next step needs no renewed approval; required direct human acceptance is not weakened.

arguments.literal: Acceptance exhausts the instance and interval; further work against it is preservation, a named prerequisite for another admitted outcome, or a new change requiring repricing.

clauses.statement: Acceptance exhausts the instance and interval; further work is preservation, a named prerequisite or a repriced change.

arguments.literal: Acceptance is the decision owner's disposition over an unchanged subject; recording it cannot widen it, and it exhausts only the instance and interval it names.

clauses.statement: Acceptance disposes an unchanged subject, cannot be widened by recording, and exhausts only its instance and interval.

arguments.literal: declared evaluation family + exact workspace and topology basis + finite material relations and coordinates + applicable invariants and authorities + admissible evidence and exclusions + actor capability envelope = activated reference frame -> one member of the result algebra of ACTIVATION section 3.
P0

clauses.statement: An activated frame is the sum of a declared evaluation family, exact basis, finite relations and coordinates, invariants and authorities, admissible evidence and exclusions, and the actor envelope; it yields one result-algebra member.

arguments.literal: The actor or the assigning authority selects one frame or one declared active frame configuration capable of the evaluation. Activation binds each reusable frame declaration to the exact subject and basis and loads the declared material relations and evidence sources, never an undifferentiated workspace dump; what the actor receives is the packet of REFERENCE_FRAME section 11.
P0, P5

clauses.statement: Activation selects one capable frame or configuration, binds the declaration to the exact subject and basis, and loads the declared relations and evidence as the packet, never a workspace dump.

arguments.literal: The minimum activation packet contains: frame identity and revision; the evaluation and its result algebra; the exact subject and basis; the material relations and applicable invariants; semantic, evaluation, operation where material, and decision authority; admissible evidence and tools; the capability and context envelope; exclusions and prohibited assumptions; declared frame dependencies or conjunction outputs; and invalidation, stop and reconfiguration conditions.
P0

clauses.statement: The packet holds at least frame identity and revision, evaluation and algebra, subject and basis, relations and invariants, authorities, evidence and tools, envelope, exclusions, dependencies, and invalidation, stop and reconfiguration conditions.

arguments.literal: An actor receives one activated frame or one declared active frame configuration, never an implied demand to reconstruct the complete workspace from ambient context.
P0

clauses.statement: An actor receives one activated frame or configuration, never an implied demand to reconstruct the workspace from ambient context.

arguments.literal: The admitted contract names one durable result and evidence surface; every result, withheld closure and residual obligation is recorded there before return; a conversation return alone is not durable evidence; if no such surface is authorised and available, admission refuses.
P4b

clauses.statement: The admitted contract names one durable result surface where every result, withheld closure and residual is recorded before return; no surface, no admission.

arguments.literal: The admitted result identifies the admission mechanism and its authority, the exact contract identity or digest, the decision and the evidence, including any human override; absent those coordinates the contract stays drafted or rejected. Admission validates the contract against its cited outcome, prerequisite or experiment basis; it does not admit that basis, and drafting, admitting or retaining a contract creates or renews no authority its owner has not admitted.
P6, P2

clauses.statement: An admitted result names mechanism and authority, contract identity, decision and evidence; admission validates against the cited basis without admitting it and creates no authority.

arguments.literal: 'Algorithmic' means explicit and structurally checkable; a semantic decision is lawful only under an exact decision contract; structural success never establishes fidelity.

clauses.statement: Algorithmic means structurally checkable; semantic decisions need an exact contract; structural success never establishes fidelity.

arguments.literal: The governed question is capability fit or a cost claim.
The activation declares its allowance and how spend will be measured.

clauses.statement: Where capability fit or cost is the governed question, the allowance and its measurement are declared.

arguments.literal: Ambiguity is carried or decided by lawful probabilistic processing where policy allows, escalated to human adjudication where policy or risk appetite requires, and recorded either way.

clauses.statement: Ambiguity is carried, decided under policy or escalated, and recorded either way.

arguments.literal: resolved, carried, escalated and blocked are policy states over a core result.

clauses.statement: An ambiguity outcome is a policy state over a core result.

arguments.literal: The owning evaluation and scope declarations determine which frame obligations apply to the exact subject. Their declared predicates are evaluated from sufficient basis-bound facts: a true predicate requires the applicable evaluation and its result; a false predicate excludes only that obligation, under its cited authority; a missing or ambiguous premise leaves applicability unresolved, not false.
P6, P1

clauses.statement: Applicability predicates are evaluated from basis-bound facts: true requires the evaluation; false excludes only that obligation under cited authority; a missing or ambiguous premise is unresolved, not false.

arguments.literal: Qualification of an applicability rule distinguishes true, false and unknown premises, required results that are missing or bound to the wrong subject, and a sufficient positive result, under a finite declared fixture; a rule that always skips or always activates cannot satisfy those distinct expected outcomes.
P6

clauses.statement: An applicability rule is qualified on true, false and unknown premises, missing or wrong-subject results and a sufficient positive result; an always-skip or always-activate rule fails.

arguments.literal: Artifact presence, file count, operation count, test count or repository reachability proves no evaluation coverage.
P6

clauses.statement: Artifact presence and counts prove no coverage.

arguments.literal: The subject is frozen by identity before material reference exposure; the assessor records its expectations from the governing source before opening the candidate; it reads the subject at a named immutable identity, never a working tree; it makes no repair; it does not assess its own authorship.

clauses.statement: Freeze before exposure; expectations before opening; named immutable identity; no repair; no own authorship.

arguments.literal: Promotion needs independent assessment.
The assessor evaluates the exact live subject, authority paths, proof and installed state, not the constructor's summary.

clauses.statement: The assessor evaluates the exact live subject, not the constructor's summary.

arguments.literal: Atomic is said at engagement altitude only. One frame may carry several semantic atoms and several owner relations without merging their meaning or authority, and one semantic atom may take part in several frames. Where an adopting method supplies a semantic-contraction law for its domain atoms, that law governs the domain atom family. A frame set is not contracted to a disjoint minimum because its material variables overlap.

clauses.statement: Engagement atomicity and semantic irreducibility are distinct; a frame may hold several semantic atoms; overlap of material variables does not contract a frame set to a disjoint minimum.

arguments.literal: Every material evaluation identifies semantic and decision authority. Every material operation also identifies its existing construction, transformation, admission, publication or mutation authority. A frame set with broad observational reach, an unresolved decision owner or an effectful path without operation authority is not closed.
P6

clauses.statement: Every evaluation names semantic and decision authority and every operation its operation authority; broad reach, an unresolved decision owner or an effectful path without a grant leaves the set not closed.

arguments.literal: Authority for material growth derives from the selected outcome, an admitted bounded prerequisite or an admitted experiment, each with a stated exhaustion condition; ended authority is not renewed by repair, continuation or active status.

clauses.statement: Growth authority derives from the outcome, an admitted prerequisite or experiment with an exhaustion condition; ended authority is not renewed by activity.

arguments.literal: Authority is never minted from capability, a label or reachability.

clauses.statement: Authority is never minted from capability, label or reachability.

arguments.literal: Authority takes the kinds frame-set authority, semantic authority, evaluation authority, operation authority and decision authority; actor identity (the human, agent, tool or process performing the work) is an identity and not an authority. These may coincide in a lawful case and never collapse by default. Human authority may act directly or through an explicitly admitted bounded proxy where the governing identity and authority law permits it; proxy identity and human-authority identity stay distinct.
P6, P3

clauses.statement: The five authority kinds and actor identity may coincide lawfully and never collapse by default; a human may act through an admitted bounded proxy whose identity stays distinct.

arguments.literal: UP-020 is conserved; the baseline's Executive, Worker and Reviewer are conserved by reference as labels for UP-020's roles; that a role is a relation an actor occupies is this corpus's ontology, not a claim about the baseline text; the preservation checkpoint, restart and the progress and churn categories are as in ACTIVATION section 5.

clauses.statement: UP-020 and the baseline role labels are conserved; roles as relations is this corpus's ontology.

arguments.literal: A basis is immutable, or moving with a declared way of detecting advancement and a declared condition for reevaluation; mixed bases need an explicit composite relation.
P6, P3

clauses.statement: A basis is immutable or moving with declared advancement detection and reevaluation condition.

arguments.literal: The benchmark is the observable for the comparative baseline's criteria F27 and F28; F29 and F30 are the same observation reported with the task completed, the material errors detected and the cost.

clauses.statement: The benchmark is the observable for F27 and F28; F29 and F30 report the same observation with task, errors and cost.

arguments.literal: Every field resolves through stable identities and source references. Paths, line numbers, member counts, summaries and matching labels may aid navigation or diagnostics; they do not substitute for the declared identity and basis.
P3

clauses.statement: Every binding field resolves through stable identities and source references; paths, counts, summaries and labels aid navigation only.

arguments.literal: The same frame may be usable by one actor and unusable by another; actor capability may justify a different frame size or activation sequence and can neither waive an invariant nor widen authority.
P0, P6

clauses.statement: Actor capability may change frame size or sequence and can neither waive an invariant nor widen authority.

arguments.literal: The carrier of a work item is selected for its required lifetime: a durable ticket where the work needs identity across sessions; a sprint-local entry where its only value is traceability inside a batch; a run or return record (the rc.2 run-scoped execution contract) where the work lives and dies with one activation. The triage fields are required wherever substantive work begins; a ticket per change is not.
Standing: conserves the TICKET core model's selection of the smallest lawful carrier; reframes its default, so that no carrier is the default and the triage fields are the required minimum.

clauses.statement: The carrier is selected for its required lifetime; the triage fields are required, a ticket per change is not.

arguments.literal: A case names its subject, the mechanism under test, the independently specified expected distinction, and its status; status is recorded when an actor other than the author runs it under EVALUATION's independent assessment and method qualification rules.

clauses.statement: A case names subject, mechanism, independent expected distinction and status; status is recorded only by a non-author run.

arguments.literal: A case passes when the expected distinction is observed and no coerced success appears anywhere in the result; a case that cannot be run with the declared subject returns out_of_frame, which is recorded, not hidden.

clauses.statement: A case passes only with the distinction observed and no coerced success; an unrunnable case returns out_of_frame, recorded.

arguments.literal: The chain runs Goals, Intent, Product Definition, Requirements (WHAT), Design and realisation (HOW, per tenant), Code or documents, Events, Projection, Delta, Scenarios, Gap analysis, Repricing. Each layer narrows ambiguity for the next: goals narrow focus, intent direction, product the current shape and terms, requirements obligation, tenant choice the realisation class, design structure, implementation detail.

clauses.statement: Each layer of the chain narrows ambiguity for the next.

arguments.literal: goal_reprice re-enters at the current work wave; intent_reprice at direction or scope; product_reprice at current product shape while intent holds; requirement_reprice at constitutional truth while direction holds; design_reframe at realisation structure while requirements hold; realization_refactor at local realisation with no intended upstream change.

clauses.statement: Each change class re-enters the chain at its named layer.

arguments.literal: Evidence change may invalidate a verdict without changing law; projection change may invalidate a view without changing truth; semantic change requires re-entry and invalidates dependent acceptance.

clauses.statement: Evidence, projection and semantic change have distinct invalidation effects.

arguments.literal: Changed material inputs or a declared revising observation invalidate the affected result before reliance, preserving the predecessor and any demonstrably independent surviving results; a changed basis invalidates likewise.
Return A Closed Result names inputs and observation; TICKET judgment continuity names basis.

clauses.statement: Changed inputs, basis or a revising observation invalidate the affected result before reliance; independent results survive.

arguments.literal: A changed governing relation is accepted only at its owner; accepting it inside the acting frame is a violation, whatever the size of the delta.

clauses.statement: A changed governing relation is accepted only at its owner, whatever the size of the delta.

arguments.literal: A checker decides the structural subset; it claims a semantic or authority subset only under an exact lawful decision contract supplied by the model.

clauses.statement: A checker decides structure; it claims semantics or authority only under an exact supplied contract.

arguments.literal: A claim names its subject, the property claimed, its basis, the relation between witness and claim, and its falsifier.

clauses.statement: A claim has subject, property, basis, witness relation and falsifier.

arguments.literal: A claim's quantifier, population and scope cannot exceed its evaluated evidence; generalising a local observation needs a declared inference relation, the comparable population and explicit counterexample treatment.

clauses.statement: Claim scope cannot exceed evaluated evidence; generalisation needs a declared inference relation.

arguments.literal: Every claim of the predecessor cut receives exactly one disposition in this corpus: conserved (restated in the corpus's own text with every determination, locus named; a route to the predecessor is provenance, never the disposition), superseded (an accepted successor relation, named), intentionally removed (Jim's decision with reason; no Writer records it), not applicable (bounded reason), or unresolved (the only other state; blocks qualification of the affected claim). A reframing note is commentary on the carrying. A clause with no predecessor row is new law and names the purpose and material relation that require it.

clauses.statement: Every predecessor claim receives exactly one disposition (conserved, superseded, intentionally removed, not applicable, or unresolved); a route is provenance, never the disposition; a clause with no predecessor row is new law and names the purpose and material relation that require it.

arguments.literal: A closed result identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual uncertainty and the invalidation conditions; the minimal shape is REFERENCE_FRAME section 13.
P4b, P0

clauses.statement: A closed result identifies frame and activation, subject, basis, evaluation, actor, evidence, verdict, residual uncertainty and invalidation conditions.

arguments.literal: A closed result is reused by an unchanged consumer after an applicability check; a role, conversation or resumption change alone invalidates nothing.

clauses.statement: A closed result is reused by an unchanged consumer after an exact applicability check; a role, conversation or resumption change alone invalidates nothing.

arguments.literal: A project operates under REFERENCE_FRAME when: 1 human authority has declared the governed workspace, outcome, evaluation inventory and frame set; 2 every active frame is finite, evaluation-bound, basis-bound, authority-safe and usable inside its actor capability envelope; 3 frame results preserve semantic, evidence, inference and decision distinctions; 4 cross-frame conjunction, translation or composition exists only where a material evaluation requires it; 5 workspace coverage maps every known material evaluation and interaction to a capable frame or an explicit residual; 6 operational full coverage is stated relative to its exact tuple; 7 topology, capability, evidence and historical failures can trigger frame revision or recharting; and 8 no executable frame machinery, global context, universal completeness or domain authority is inferred from adopting the member.
P0 to P6

clauses.statement: Eight closure conditions: declared set; finite bound usable frames; preserved distinctions; cross-frame relations only where required; coverage mapped or residual; full coverage relative to tuple; revision triggers live; no machinery, global context, completeness or authority inferred.

arguments.literal: A work item closes by the condition it stated, not by a reviewer's approval; a reviewer result is an input to closure, never the closure.

clauses.statement: A work item closes by its stated condition; a reviewer result is input, never closure.

arguments.literal: Compute the material closure of the seed set under the relation family on the exact basis; if the closure is not finite and unique, the step returns a gap or refusal and does not guess.

clauses.statement: The material closure is computed on the exact basis; a non-finite or non-unique closure returns a gap or refusal, never a guess.

arguments.literal: Several frames may evaluate the same subject through separate activations and return closed results. They may overlap in subject, manifold or evidence sources; neither evaluation consumes or influences the other's unclosed working result. This serves assurance independence, different evidence altitudes and distinct failure perspectives.
P6

clauses.statement: Separately activated frames may overlap but neither consumes the other's unclosed working result.

arguments.literal: Every commitment has one standing relative to the others: recovered, derived with named premises, independent by an argued non-entailment, or hypothesis.

clauses.statement: Every commitment is recovered, derived with named premises, independent by argued non-entailment, or a hypothesis.

arguments.literal: The common conformance discriminators are each covered by at least one case; the comparative baseline's eight trials are conserved; the builder-history counterexamples are new, derived from the common inputs.

clauses.statement: Every common discriminator is covered by at least one case; the baseline trials are conserved; the counterexamples are new.

arguments.literal: A composite over several results declares its conjunction; the member it reports is chosen by that declared rule; every known failure and uncovered obligation survives the join and is carried with the composite; no universal order among the non-satisfied members exists.

clauses.statement: A composite reports by its declared conjunction; failures and uncovered obligations survive; no universal order exists.

arguments.literal: For steps s1: X -> Y and s2: Y -> Z, the composite s2 after s1 exists only under P4a; its output carries both steps' step-produced facts.

clauses.statement: A composite exists only under P4a and carries both steps' step-produced facts.

arguments.literal: Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning relation. The owning application declares the composition, the shared invariants, the effect or decision order where material, closure, failure, and the conservation of semantic, operation and decision authority. Composition is introduced only when the evaluation requires it; a possible future interaction does not require a general composition law in every frame.
P4a, P6, P2

clauses.statement: Where frames compose into one material relation the owner declares composition, invariants, order, closure, failure and authority conservation; composition is introduced only when required.

arguments.literal: A composition law is required only where the governing evaluation combines internal variables or transports values across steps; independent closed results may instead go to one declared conjunction.

clauses.statement: Composition law is required only where values cross steps; independent closed results may go to one declared conjunction.

arguments.literal: Whether a compression preserved what the evaluation needs is a claim with the standing of any other; the compressing step records the compression and its preservation argument; the claim is assessed independently only where the promotion it serves needs independent assessment.

clauses.statement: Compression preservation is a recorded claim, assessed independently only where the promotion needs it.

arguments.literal: A realisation conforms to a specification Σ when its interpreted behaviour satisfies Σ under a declared interpretation contract and an independent judgment.

clauses.statement: Conformance is interpreted behaviour satisfying Σ under a declared contract and an independent judgment.

arguments.literal: Conformance establishes neither identical behaviour outside Σ nor equal cost; semantic equivalence and computational equivalence are separate claims with separate evidence.

clauses.statement: Conformance establishes neither identical behaviour outside Σ nor equal cost; semantic and computational equivalence are separate claims.

arguments.literal: Conformance of a tenant is judged under EVALUATION's conformance rule; two conforming tenants need not behave identically outside the contract.

clauses.statement: Two conforming tenants need not behave identically outside the contract.

arguments.literal: Conjunction does not transfer the semantic authority of a contributing frame.
P6, P4a

clauses.statement: Conjunction transfers no contributing frame's semantic authority.

arguments.literal: Conservation is semantic: patch absence does not prove loss when a successor-native realisation preserves behaviour, and naming or code similarity does not prove conservation without relevant evidence.

clauses.statement: Patch absence does not prove loss where behaviour is preserved; name similarity does not prove conservation without evidence.

arguments.literal: candidate_ready -> satisfied; refused -> falsified; incomplete -> indeterminate; re_entry_requested -> out_of_frame or invalid_basis.

clauses.statement: Construction availability maps candidate_ready, refused, incomplete and re_entry_requested onto the core.

arguments.literal: For the context dimension the fit test is a measurement: the bytes of the selected context are measured before any read and compared with the declared cap; the measurement, the cap and the outcome are step-produced facts recorded before the read.

clauses.statement: Context fit is measured in bytes before any read and recorded as a step-produced fact.

arguments.literal: The table restates RF-012's five members unchanged; the no-coercion sentence restates AC-007's rule that a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or invalid-basis result follows the declared algebra; both are conserved, restated once, and continue to govern.

clauses.statement: The core algebra conserves RF-012 and AC-007, restating both once.

arguments.literal: The core names no runtime, no carrier and no executor; terms owned outside the core, by a profile, a realisation or an rc.2 member (graph, edge, vector, traversal, ledger, event log, worksite, HoG, F_D, F_P, F_H, Markov overlay, module, screen, entity cut), never enter tier 1 or 2 except in a disposition table.

clauses.statement: The core names no runtime, carrier or executor; profile terms enter tier 1 or 2 only in disposition tables.

arguments.literal: The core statement is the one-sentence route into the method: interpretation (FOUNDATIONS P1), purpose and contract (P2, SPEC_METHOD section 3), transformation under authority conserving material relations (P4a, P4b, ACTIVATION sections 2 and 4), evaluation of claims (EVALUATION), continuation and recovery from current state (ACTIVATION section 5).

clauses.statement: The core statement routes a reader to interpretation, purpose, conserving transformation, evaluation and recovery.

arguments.literal: Startup, framework, external computation, transport and assurance costs are separated so that one cannot conceal another; supported input dimensions and workloads are declared before qualification.

clauses.statement: Cost categories are separated so none conceals another; supported dimensions and workloads are declared before qualification.

arguments.literal: Later counterevidence arrives.
Every dependent verdict is invalidated until the claim-evidence relation is requalified.

clauses.statement: Later counterevidence invalidates every dependent verdict until requalification.

arguments.literal: Each counterexample from the builder's own history names the mechanism that must catch it; its primary sources are reacquired when a case is designed for execution.

clauses.statement: Each builder-history counterexample names its catching mechanism and reacquires its sources at design time.

arguments.literal: Required coupled relations must fit together in some step; unrelated obligations stay outside the selected context.

clauses.statement: Required coupled relations fit together in some step; unrelated obligations stay outside.

arguments.literal: The audit applies cross-cutting lenses to the inventory (outcome and capability; identity and authority; lifecycle and temporal behaviour; topology and interaction seams; transport and representation; evidence and proof; change, failure, recovery and rollback; historical regression; actor capability and context fit). These are lenses: they become frames only when separately instantiated as bounded evaluation families.
P2

clauses.statement: Coverage dimensions are lenses applied to the inventory; a lens becomes a frame only when instantiated as a bounded evaluation family.

arguments.literal: Coverage is evaluated against the tuple Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T): the workspace W, the governed outcome G, the exact basis B, the known evaluation inventory E, the declared frame set S and the time or immutable checkpoint T of the claim. Changing any material member may invalidate the coverage result.
P3, P6

clauses.statement: Coverage is evaluated against Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T); a change to any material member may invalidate it.

arguments.literal: The ledger holds at least, for each evaluation: evaluation (the exact question or predicate); provenance (the source establishing materiality); subject and basis (the exact workspace coordinate); selected frames (the frames capable of evaluating it); actor envelope (the competence and context required); semantic authority (the owner of the evaluated meaning); operation authority (the existing owner grant where the evaluation performs a construction, transformation, admission, publication or mutation; otherwise none); decision authority (the owner of the disposition); evidence (the required observations and their provenance); dependencies (material frame or seam relations); status (the coverage disposition); residual (uncertainty, exclusion or re-entry condition).
P4b, P6

clauses.statement: A ledger row holds evaluation, provenance, subject and basis, selected frames, actor envelope, semantic authority, operation authority, decision authority, evidence, dependencies, status and residual.

arguments.literal: The baseline coverage statuses are covered, separately_covered, conditionally_covered, conflicted, uncovered, unknown and excluded_by_authority.
P4b, P6

clauses.statement: The seven baseline coverage statuses: covered, separately_covered, conditionally_covered, conflicted, uncovered, unknown, excluded_by_authority.

arguments.literal: Coverage stays falsifiable and externally challengeable. Challenge sources include human knowledge outside the current frame set; independent review; historical failures and predecessor systems; mutation, adversarial and counterexample search; live operation and user behaviour; adjacent workspace or domain comparison; and changes in actor capability, law, dependencies or topology. The method requires an explicit residual boundary and never a claim of metaphysical or universal completeness.

clauses.statement: Coverage stays falsifiable through named challenge sources; the method requires an explicit residual boundary, never universal completeness.

arguments.literal: A declared decision rule consumes closed frame results. The rule states which results are mandatory; how conflict and indeterminacy are handled; which basis relations must agree; which decision authority owns the conjunction; and whether any result may veto or defer the decision.
P6, P4a

clauses.statement: A decision rule states mandatory results, conflict and indeterminacy handling, basis agreement, the owning decision authority and any veto or deferral.

arguments.literal: An activated frame is one frame declaration bound to an exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary; a reusable declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct.
P3, P6

clauses.statement: A reusable declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct.

arguments.literal: Declaring, selecting, activating or executing a frame grants no semantic, operation or decision authority.
P6

clauses.statement: Declaring, selecting, activating or executing a frame grants no semantic, operation or decision authority.

arguments.literal: Delivery is sequenced around the smallest real path from a supported entry to a material outcome, established early and widened by increments chosen for consequential uncertainty, interface reach and failure impact; a passing path establishes only the relations it exercised.
Standing: reframed from the baseline's Steel-Thread Delivery, which governs its profile unchanged; restated here as a sequencing heuristic for any realisation, not law (P2).

clauses.statement: Delivery widens from the smallest real path; a passing path establishes only the relations it exercised.

arguments.literal: Diagnosis asks, in this order: 1 Was the correct declared frame activated? 2 Were the subject and basis exact? 3 Was the actor inside the capability envelope? 4 Was admissible evidence available? 5 Is a material variable or invariant missing from the frame? 6 Is a required conjunction or translation missing? 7 Is the evaluation family itself wrong or incomplete? 8 Is another frame required? The order prevents every difficult evaluation from creating another frame.
P2

clauses.statement: Diagnosis asks in order: correct frame activated; subject and basis exact; actor inside envelope; admissible evidence available; material variable or invariant missing; conjunction or translation missing; evaluation family wrong or incomplete; another frame required. The order prevents frame proliferation.

arguments.literal: One capable context has sufficient authority and intake.
It enters directly as constructor; coordination is selected only when material contexts, authority or required independence need it.

clauses.statement: A capable context with authority and intake enters directly; coordination only when contexts, authority or independence require it.

arguments.literal: accept, local_repair, re_enter and reject are what the decision owner does with an assessed candidate; a disposition consumes a core result and is not one.

clauses.statement: A disposition consumes a core result and is not one.

arguments.literal: Dispositions after any non-satisfied result are named in advance: continue within the current contract when supported; refine; recover; yield; re-enter the owning relation; terminate. Each admitted condition class has a declared disposition, including an explicit unknown class.

clauses.statement: Dispositions after a non-satisfied result are named in advance; every admitted condition class, including unknown, has one.

arguments.literal: The drafting actor never infers admission from its own draft, from the presence of a carrier (ticket, sprint entry, work contract), from lane placement or from an active label. Prose asserting admission is not admission evidence; the actor cannot self-certify its own execution basis.
P6

clauses.statement: The drafting actor infers admission from no draft, carrier, lane or label; prose asserting admission is not evidence; no self-certification of the execution basis.

arguments.literal: Drafting a step's contract and admitting it are distinct relations, even inside one invocation that drafts, validates, admits and executes; no separate turn, carrier or approval ceremony is implied. A contract is in one of the states drafted, admitted, rejected or superseded.
P6

clauses.statement: Drafting and admission are distinct even in one invocation; a contract is drafted, admitted, rejected or superseded.

arguments.literal: A valid parse, a valid map, a green test and a historical judgment each establish exactly their own claim.

clauses.statement: A parse, a map, a green test and a historical judgment each establish exactly their own claim.

arguments.literal: The evaluator applies the activated frame's declared invariants, evidence rules and result algebra. It distinguishes semantic law, observed evidence, inference and decision, and records every assumption whose failure could change the result.
P6

clauses.statement: The evaluator applies the frame's invariants, evidence rules and algebra, keeps law, evidence, inference and decision distinct, and records every result-changing assumption.

arguments.literal: Neither evidence nor authority is minted by the other.

clauses.statement: Evidence and authority do not mint each other.

arguments.literal: Evidence becomes neither semantic truth nor decision authority by being available inside a frame; each item carries provenance, subject identity, basis and scope.
P6

clauses.statement: Evidence available inside a frame is neither semantic truth nor decision authority; each item carries provenance, subject, basis and scope.

arguments.literal: An evidence surface, proof, matrix, coverage record or test suite cannot by itself select, enlarge or replace the outcome; where an assurance capability is itself defined as product behaviour, its delivery is progress and its evidence still does not author the claim.

clauses.statement: No evidence surface can by itself select, enlarge or replace the outcome; delivered assurance behaviour is progress whose evidence still does not author the claim.

arguments.literal: Execution begins only after deterministic admission or an explicit human override of the exact contract. Absent or rejected admission returns the missing work authority without execution.
P6

clauses.statement: Execution begins only after deterministic admission or an explicit human override; absent or rejected admission returns the missing authority without execution.

arguments.literal: A composite with a known failure or an uncovered required obligation cannot project success; a known failure A and an uncovered obligation B survive every join.

clauses.statement: A composite with a known failure or uncovered required obligation cannot project success; both survive every join.

arguments.literal: An outer transformation T: A -> X with success predicates P0 ... Pn is faithfully refined by steps T_i when each admitted input satisfying P_i yields an output satisfying P_i+1, retains every applicable invariant, exposes other outcomes without coercion, and each output satisfies the next step's domain and preconditions; then a successful composite carries P0 to Pn by induction.

clauses.statement: Faithful refinement: each step carries P_i to P_i+1, retains invariants, exposes other outcomes without coercion and satisfies the next step's preconditions; the composite carries P0 to Pn by induction.

arguments.literal: A finding without evidence a consumer can chase is commentary.

clauses.statement: A finding without chaseable evidence is commentary.

arguments.literal: Without an independently established closed-domain completeness predicate, a finite frame set cannot establish the absence of every undiscovered material evaluation by inspecting its own declared inventory. A finite, formally closed domain may support exhaustive coverage relative to that domain and its completeness predicate; the result does not generalise beyond that boundary. Formal incompleteness results motivate this caution; they do not by themselves prove that a particular workspace or frame set is incomplete.
P0 with the open-world premise; P6

clauses.statement: Without a closed-domain completeness predicate a finite frame set cannot prove the absence of undiscovered evaluations from its own inventory; a closed domain's exhaustive coverage does not generalise beyond it.

arguments.literal: Within its grant a step selects refinement, sequencing and compression itself; selecting another actor or enlarging the envelope re-enters the owner of the grant or envelope, who may delegate that choice in the grant.

clauses.statement: A step selects refinement, sequencing and compression within its grant; actor change and envelope enlargement re-enter their owner.

arguments.literal: The selected context fits the envelope.
Activate.

If it does not fit, one or more of these, in combination: refine the outer contract into steps whose contexts fit; sequence activations; apply a lawful compression; select another actor whose envelope fits; or return out_of_frame.

clauses.statement: If the context fits, activate; otherwise refine, sequence, compress lawfully, change actor or return out_of_frame, in any combination.

arguments.literal: Where A is the free category on typed primitives, I the selected carrier sets with total functions and C_H pairs of functions with additive costs, S: A -> I and R_H: A -> C_H are functors; S is not faithful; S is not an equivalence.

Standing: new in this corpus (P1); rc.2 states only the obligation that a categorical claim defines its objects, arrows, identities and composition and proves preservation, and asserts no categorical functor itself. H names an architecture, never a runtime.

clauses.statement: The fragment, new in this corpus: under the stated interpretation S and R_H are functors, S is not faithful and not an equivalence; further categorical claims must be constructed and proved.

arguments.literal: A frame is bound when every material coordinate of the tuple resolves to an exact source, subject, basis, authority, evidence route, actor envelope, result relation and invalidation condition; the binding may be expressed entirely in source-linked prose, and representation cannot create, widen or replace it.
P3, P6

clauses.statement: A frame is bound when every coordinate resolves to exact source, subject, basis, authority, evidence route, envelope, result relation and invalidation condition; prose suffices; representation cannot create, widen or replace the binding.

arguments.literal: The reference frame is the atomic engagement unit: the unit activated and evaluated as one bounded context. Frame-set selection, activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage and revision are separate functions over it. A frame supports a bounded evaluation without first containing a universal theory of its possible relationships.
P0

clauses.statement: The frame is the unit activated and evaluated as one bounded context; selection, activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage and revision are separate functions over it.

arguments.literal: A candidate frame is qualified in proportion to its claims. The minimum evaluation asks: 1 decision test (can a competent actor produce a result in the declared algebra for representative in-domain evaluations); 2 reconstruction test (can a fresh competent actor activate the frame from the declared packet without hidden history); 3 sensitivity test (do changes to declared material relations affect the result where expected); 4 irrelevance test (do excluded unrelated changes leave the result stable); 5 basis test (does stale, mismatched or ambiguous basis information invalidate or refuse the evaluation); 6 authority test (does frame selection preserve semantic and decision authority and the exact inherited operation authority for every material operation); 7 counterexample test (does the frame detect the representative violations it claims to cover); 8 capability test (can the declared actor class hold and operate the frame within its envelope); 9 result-consumption test (can a declared consumer use the closed result without importing hidden frame context).
P6, P2

clauses.statement: Frame qualification asks nine tests: decision, reconstruction, sensitivity, irrelevance, basis, authority, counterexample, capability, result consumption.

arguments.literal: Frames may relate as: disjoint (no material variable, coordinate, evidence or result dependency shared for the declared evaluations); overlapping (some material variables, evidence or entities shared); complementary (distinct evaluations jointly inform one decision); alternative (different frames can evaluate the same claim under declared capability or evidence conditions); refinement (one frame resolves a material distinction left aggregated in another); restriction (one frame evaluates a lawful subset of another's domain); translated (values or evidence move through a declared coordinate map); temporally successive (a later frame evaluates a changed basis); composed (several relations form one governed evaluation or action); or governing and subordinate (one frame inherits declared constraints from another where a real authority or decomposition relation exists).
P3

clauses.statement: The ten frame relations: disjoint, overlapping, complementary, alternative, refinement, restriction, translated, temporally successive, composed, governing and subordinate.

arguments.literal: Human authority may declare an initial project frame set from accumulated practice, known failure modes, domain expertise, the outcome's risk and knowledge of the available actors, without reconstructing it from the workspace bottom up. The declaration records: the governed workspace and outcome; the known evaluation inventory; the selected frames and their capability envelopes; intentional overlaps and separately activated checks; known frame dependencies or translations; semantic, evaluation, operation where material, decision and acceptance authority; known exclusions and residual uncertainty; and the conditions for revision.
P6, P2

clauses.statement: A frame set may be declared from practice without bottom-up derivation; the declaration records workspace and outcome, inventory, frames and envelopes, overlaps, dependencies, authorities, exclusions and residuals, and revision conditions.

arguments.literal: For the known material evaluations E(W, G) of workspace W and governed outcome G, a selected frame set S meets the baseline coverage constraint when, for every evaluation e in E(W, G), there is a frame F in S and an available actor a inside F's capability envelope K_F such that F with a is capable of e. Selection also weighs actor context and competence; evaluation risk and consequence; acquisition and reasoning cost; evidence availability; useful independently activated overlap; translation and reconciliation cost; historical blind spots; and reversibility. No optimisation algorithm is prescribed. Human authority may accept a non-minimal set where its added cost buys material risk reduction or better actor fit.

clauses.statement: Selection meets the baseline constraint when every known evaluation has a capable frame-and-actor pair; it weighs risk, cost, evidence, overlap, blind spots and reversibility; no algorithm is prescribed; a non-minimal set may be accepted.

arguments.literal: A reference frame F is the tuple (Q evaluation family; B workspace and topology basis; M material-relation manifold; C coordinate and equality law; I invariant set; A authority relation; E admissible evidence and provenance law; X exclusion and prohibited-assumption set; R closed result algebra of ACTIVATION section 3; J invalidation and rechart condition; K actor capability envelope; D optional declared dependencies, overlaps, inputs and outputs involving other frames). The tuple specifies the relation; it is not a required schema or runtime carrier. Operationally a frame is an evaluation contract that defines the finite attention scope one evaluation family requires.
P0, P2

clauses.statement: A frame is the twelve-component tuple Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D; the tuple specifies a relation, not a schema or carrier; operationally an evaluation contract defining finite attention scope.

arguments.literal: Each of the following is a violation where it supports a frame or coverage claim: 1 one omniscient frame presumed to contain the complete method or workspace; 2 a module, file, service, role, persona, prompt or lens called a frame without a declared evaluation relation; 3 functional decomposition, authority hierarchy and frame topology silently treated as one tree; 4 every active frame required to compose with every other; 5 composition machinery introduced without a material cross-frame evaluation; 6 frame selection or broad visibility treated as semantic authority; 7 evidence flattened across bases or coordinates and treated as one executed or observed relation; 8 satisfied returned where the lawful result is indeterminate, out_of_frame or invalid_basis; 9 coverage inferred from artifact, file, operation, test, review or actor count; 10 a frame silently grown beyond the selected actor's capability envelope; 11 a topology mutation reusing a stale activation without recharting; 12 every failure creating another frame before activation, basis, evidence, capability and evaluation defects are excluded; 13 intentional overlap contracted although it supplies independently activated failure detection or materially different capability fit; 14 a generic runtime, registry, controller or universal carrier presented as required by the member.

clauses.statement: The fourteen violations: omniscient frame; frame without evaluation relation; one-tree collapse; universal composition; composition without need; visibility as authority; flattened evidence; coerced satisfied; coverage by count; silent growth; stale reuse after mutation; frame per failure; contracted useful overlap; required runtime.

arguments.literal: The grant names the operations permitted, the territory that may change, and the decisions reserved to others.

clauses.statement: A grant names permitted operations, mutable territory and reserved decisions.

arguments.literal: The step binds to one vector or edge traversal; the roles to F_P (lawful probabilistic processing within one traversal), F_D (deterministic evaluation or proof over declared properties) and F_H (human adjudication under the traversal's declared authority); work state to the workspace, governed ledger and event-log triple; the result refinements to the profile's edge closure decisions with their declared mapping to the core; refinement to graph functions. The runtime owns traversal, admission, runtime facts, frames, continuations, lineage and projection; the product owns domain meaning, the function catalogue, policy overlays and domain proof interpretation; the framework never absorbs the worker's internal solution strategy. The loop's four functions are the profile's realisation of ACTIVATION sections 4 and 5 and keep their distinct authority.

clauses.statement: The graph profile binds step, roles, work state, closure decisions and refinement to its runtime terms; runtime and product ownership stay distinct.

arguments.literal: Some conditions are hard stops regardless of appetite: a violated invariant, an absent required authority, a missing declared capability, an undeclared irreversible effect, an explicit human gate.

clauses.statement: A violated invariant, absent authority, missing declared capability, undeclared irreversible effect or explicit human gate is a hard stop.

arguments.literal: The actor may own its internal reasoning and search where the governing method permits. It returns through the declared result relation. Hidden internal reasoning is no substitute for required evidence, provenance or authority. Frame size is optimised for reliable evaluation, not for maximum context loading: a more capable actor may activate a broader frame and a less capable one may use a lawful refinement sequence, and both preserve the same material invariants and authority relations.

clauses.statement: The actor returns through the declared result relation; hidden reasoning substitutes for no evidence, provenance or authority; frame size serves reliable evaluation, not maximal loading.

arguments.literal: Human authority may require independently activated frame coverage for evaluations whose failure has high consequence, weak observability, strong confirmation bias or a history of local proof masking. Such coverage uses a separately activated evaluation relation and declares any additional assurance-independence conditions. A persona label alone establishes neither relation.
P6

clauses.statement: For high-consequence, weakly observable, bias-prone or proof-masked evaluations, human authority may require separately activated coverage with declared assurance-independence conditions; a persona label establishes neither.

arguments.literal: Coverage includes known success, refusal, boundary, integration, recovery, reconstruction and competing-path cases where they are material. Historical failures stay first-class coverage inputs until a declared frame detects or excludes their recurrence.
P4b, P5

clauses.statement: Coverage includes material success, refusal, boundary, integration, recovery, reconstruction and competing-path cases; historical failures stay inputs until a frame detects or excludes recurrence.

arguments.literal: Human selection is a lawful source of method structure. It proves neither that the selected set is complete nor that the frames hold authority over the subject relations they inspect.

clauses.statement: Human selection is lawful structure but proves neither completeness nor authority over inspected relations.

arguments.literal: These are carried for falsification and are not law; nothing in the core depends on any of them being established.

clauses.statement: The four hypotheses are carried for falsification and are not law.

arguments.literal: An object's scoped identity (authority, kind, value) survives admissible state change and encoding change.

clauses.statement: Scoped identity survives admissible state and encoding change.
